newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Gasunie to seal first N. Sea gas deal within month.
newsitem.headline: Gasunie to seal first N. Sea gas deal within month.

text.p: Dutch Gasunie said on Friday it expected to conclude within a month its first deal to buy North Sea gas via the Interconnector.
"We are on the edge of closing a deal with a player in the North Sea.... and the gas will come via the Interconnector," said company spokesman Abraham Warner.
The gas is required to supply Italy's SNAM with whom Gasunie today announced it had signed two long term supply deals.

Gasunie has agreed to deliver more than 80 billion cubic metres (bcm) of natural gas to SNAM, the gas subsidiary of ENI, from the year 2000. It has also prolonged an existing contract by six years, adding another 40 billion cubic metres to the contract.
The total 120 bcm of gas is worth about 19 billion guilders ($9.6 billion).
Gasunie said the SNAM deal would have a neutral effect on Dutch natural gas reserves, the gas coming from elsewhere.
It represents a new step in Gasunie's attempts to become a leading player in a liberalised European energy market and its gradual shift from simple gas supplier to trading company.

Last September, the Dutch government granted Gasunie permission to increase its export contracts by 240 bcm and its imports by 120 bcm, allowing Gasunie to prolong many of contracts by five to six years.
The 40 bcm extension of the existing SNAM contract is part of this larger allowance.

The 120 bcm of imports are largely accounted for. Russia's Gazprom will supply some 80 bcm and Gasunie expects to have a further 40 bcm over the next 20 years as it loses domestic market share to competitors.
The SNAM deal adds a requirement for a further 80 bcm, which in the initial stages at least, seem likely to come from the U.K. and Norwegian reserves in the North Sea.
Gasunie is 50 percent owned by the Dutch state and 25 percent each by Royal Dutch /Shell and Exxon.
